Subject: QBR playbook: infra levers & GPU unit economics — prep materials request

Team —

QBR next Tuesday: execs want a tight playbook that ties capacity levers to unit economics (GPU $/token, utilization, batching/caching impacts) and the recommended asks for Aurora’s renewal conversation. I need a 1-slide summary + backup appendix we can drop into the packet by EOD Monday.

Ask: please pull the best available data for the items below and drop into the shared doc (link below). I’ll synthesize.

Key required datapoints (minimal):
- Last 90d GPU spend by cluster (by model family if available) — actual $ and % of total infra spend.
- Average and 95p latency vs config (batch sizes, quantization variants).
- Effective tokens-per-second per-GPU under typical PL endpoints (p50/p95).
- Cache hit rate uplift measured from prefix/KV caching experiments and estimated $ savings.
- Batching experiments: throughput uplift and tail latency tradeoffs for batching windows 10–200ms.

Deliverables:
- 1-slide summary: 3 bullets (levers, numbers, ask for leadership: credit/discount ask or capacity commitment recommendation).
- Appendix: spreadsheet with raws + short notes on assumptions.

Attachments: I’ll attach my starter workbook (qbr_gpu_spend_breakdown.xlsx) to seed values.

Ben

2) For cost ask: do we propose a committed-monthly draw (reserved cores) vs a spike buffer credit structure?

Quick results from last week’s batching/caching experiment (summary below). Dropping a short PDF with charts.

Headline: prefix/KV caching delivered a 22–27% effective token-cost reduction on steady-state inference for Aurora’s prompt mix (high prefix overlap). That’s before any batching changes.

Batching tradeoffs (aurora-dev-1 cluster):
- Window 25ms: +18% throughput, median latency +9ms, p95 latency neutral.
- Window 100ms: +42% throughput, median latency +36ms, p95 latency +180ms. Not acceptable for interactive product paths.
- Combining caching + conservative batching (25–40ms) hits ~35% cost reduction without violating p95 SLA in our test.

Notes: quantization (4-bit) helped throughput ~12% but increased tail artifacts in generation for some prompt templates; risk should be called out as possible quality regression.

Attachments: batching_experiment_summary.pdf (2.1MB)

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Director, Serving Runtime & Cost Optimization

Adding scenario outputs — see infra_scenarios_v2.csv (Monica’s file) and my notes inline in the shared doc. Short summary for the packet:
- Scenario A (conservative): Recommend 10% committed capacity increase (Reserved) + 25ms batching cap + enable prefix caching on routes with >40% reuse. Estimated 12–18% unit-cost reduction; minimal latency delta.
- Scenario B (aggressive): 20% committed + 100ms batching windows + 4-bit quantization on compatible models. Estimated 28–35% unit-cost reduction but expect measurable p95 regressions on heavy prompts and a risk bucket for quality.

Operational asks for sales/CS to include in renewal: 1) ability to convert 30% of hosted spend to reserved over next 6 months, 2) 90-day testing window for quantization on subset of traffic, 3) rolling credits if p95 exceeds threshold during rollout.

Also: we should include a model-level token cost table (tokens-per-second per GPU) — I can produce that this afternoon.

Karthik
